title: Wee & Woo
description: If you can't tell Wee from Woo, then the one standing next to Wee is Woo, and the one next to Woo is Wee. Still can't tell? Well, it doesn't really matter. They're always together. You'll rarely see them alone. People natu Rally treat them as one person. Twins this in sync are rare—eating together, sleeping together, being silly together… even going to war together. When Wee & Woo enter the battlefield, they become a nightmare. No one can lock onto them. All you see is a nimble cannon roaming the field, firing powerful shells from every direction, crushing both enemy formations and their hope. "Woo is the smartest person in the world! Ever since we were kids, he's always scored full marks! And he invents amazing things—like this cannon we're using now. He designed and improved it all by himself. Me? I just help out… Anyway, Woo is a genius!" Whenever someone asks Wee about Woo, he can go on praising him for days, completely ignoring Woo blushing beside him. "Wee is amazing. He's strong and fast, unlike me… He's also really brave. Whenever there's danger, he steps forward first, unlike me… And he's kind. If someone needs help, he'll always be there, unlike me… Wee is the best person in the world!" Shy Woo only becomes this talkative when speaking about Wee. At those moments, Wee always looks at him with gentle eyes. "I don't want to be with you anymore!" No one knows who said it first, but Wee & Woo did separate once. "Without me holding him back, he'll have an easier life." They both thought the same thing. For a while after that, they lived on their own. Without Wee, Woo struggled to move his equipment. He couldn't even speak up when buying supplies, and his experiments came to a halt. Without Woo, Wee clumsily fixed his armor and counted expenses on his fingers, turning his home into a mess. "I can't live without Wee (Woo)." In the end, they went back to being inseparable, as if nothing had ever happened.

title: Yang
description: In the frozen wilds, " Yang" is more than just a name. It's a legend carried on every icy wind. They call her the "Winter Huntress," and her reputation echoes across the endless snowfields. People trust Yang, not only because she can track any beast or find her way through the worst storms, but because she never loses her head, no matter how dire things get. In a crisis, she's the first to take charge. Whether it's finding shelter, reading the winds, or building a fire, she's always steady and never rattled. Even when danger closes in, she makes tough calls without hesitation, calmly organizing everyone's escape. The harsh polar climate hasn't worn her down. If anything, it's made her even more clearheaded and unshakable under pressure. But don't mistake her for some grim, silent type. Yang has a mischievous streak. She'll crack a joke around the campfire or build a goofy snowman with her board just to get a laugh. Her chilly sense of humor is legendary, and her jokes help keep everyone's spirits up, even in the coldest nights. She knows better than anyone that out here, losing your nerve is far more dangerous than any blizzard. A century ago, the polar regions were just a distant frontier. A cold land, yes, but they were home to thriving communities. The royal oracles once urged the kingdom's fleets to sail north, and for many years, the two lands built strong ties by sharing supplies and aid. Those were prosperous times, with endless convoys heading into the snow. But one fateful day, a fleet found its way blocked by shifting ice. Only then did people realize a terrible storm had struck the polar lands. Seas froze, the cold deepened, and entire villages vanished beneath the snow. Thankfully, those earlier alliances helped some survive. But soon, the polar seas were sealed in ice, cutting off all travel and trade. Years later, when the ice finally began to thaw, a group journeyed south, only to find the kingdom gone. Rebels had torn it apart. Royal bloodlines were scattered and forced to live in hiding. The crown was lost, but the burden of old grudges remained. That night, the elders of the polar lands gathered in secret. After a long, heavy silence, they made their choice: someone must go and seek out the last of the royal line. Oh, how the bards love to sing of her, lutes in hand, in the dusky twilight. "Winter mountain sent, Boots of snow, Not knowing which way to go, Told by stars where to follow, Oh, the road is long, But still she must sing on and on. North wind blowing, Bonfire sowing, Lost footprints flowing, 'Till she knew where she was going. Oh, to raise a glass to hope, To laugh as long as winter's snow, 'Til she knows which way to go, Joined to a fantasy that never overflows, goes or slows... The wind still howled outside, the fire crackled in the darkness. Yang packed her things for the journey, fumbling with the straps, clearly lost in thought. "The place you're headed won't be any kinder than these frozen plains," the elder said softly. "Right now, you don't seem like the legendary Huntress. What's troubling you?" Yang looked up. "...I worry that if things are too different out there, I'll end up changing too much..." The elder pulled his coat tighter, a gentle smile on his face. "There's nothing wrong with change. Life's a voyage, and every sea you cross leaves its mark on your ship. To keep going, you patch it up and sail on." He looked Yang in the eye. "When friends drift away, you learn to take the first step. When family tests your patience, you learn to stand on your own. When no one seems to notice your efforts, you start to doubt yourself." Yang sat in silence. The elder poked the fire, making the flames leap higher. "But what makes a ship itself isn't the wood it's built from, but that it always knows where it's headed." Outside, the storm still raged. Yang fastened her board to her pack, her eyes full of resolve. The path to legend was waiting, and she was ready to face it.

title: Yeonwoo
description: Yeonwoo is a passionate swordswoman, admired by all for her meticulous nature and sharp eye. She has an uncanny ability to see things from a unique perspective, likely due to her extensive travels and broadened horizons. Whether friend or foe, it is wise to always stay on high alert when you are around Yeonwoo. "Accomplishing something is hard, but ruining it is easy." This is the principle Yeonwoo has lived by her whole life. During her journeys, she saw many abandon their Convictions in pursuit of short-term gain. Most people understand the value of perseverance, but few truly practice it. "A blade must be honed a thousand times to be sharp, and a dance takes a lifetime of dedication to master." Yeonwoo weaves this principle of swordsmanship into every aspect of her daily life. Yeonwoo first held a sword at the age of five—a ceremonial blade that stood taller than she did. While other children were still busy playing and roughhousing, she rose early each morning, practicing her stance with quiet determination. She tirelessly repeated the routine day after day, each session lasting for a few hours. It wasn't until a year later that her master, who was also her father, finally taught her the most basic moves. At that moment, no one could have foreseen the remarkable things she would go on to achieve in the future. Yeonwoo trains in autumn to absorb the spirit of fallen petals and races through stormy nights to emulate the grace of swallows. She incorporates everything she has seen and heard into her dance. Each time she executes her moves, she reconnects with her beliefs and purpose. Each time she sheaths her sword, she quiets her restlessness with calm. Yeonwoo believes that the vast insights gained from her travels, intertwined with her skills, will one day give rise to the ultimate dance—one that embodies the heart and soul of the world.

title: Zoe
description: Zoe manifests her emotional states not through words or actions, but through her magical hair... According to Amadeus, her hair has reflected her mood since she was young. While black signifies her patience as she waits to strike at her prey, yellow reflects her exhilaration as she starts hunting. Zoe channels the energy of every cell in her body to chase down her prey, ultimately tearing them apart. Zoe isn't a noble knight or an elegant archer, but an adopted child of the Unjust League just like Amadeus. Born with immense strength, Zoe always charges to the frontline of battles, relishing the exhilaration each wound brings and taking pleasure in raw, physical contact. Ruthless in her attacks, Zoe is willing to go to any lengths to secure victory, even if it means being seen as a villain. To her, winning is everything, and honor holds little value. Zoe was raised in a suburban area north of Noxholm, a region bordering a forest and home to the destitute. Yet, even there, Zoe wasn't spared from the exorbitant taxes, the nobles who tormented the common folk for amusement, and the fanatical cults eager to spread their influence. She also witnessed countless betrayals and backstabbing, even within families. The underprivileged, regarded as insignificant by the nobility, were willing to pay any price just to survive another day. It was in this harsh reality that Zoe realized the necessity of becoming stronger—so she could call the shots in this unforgiving society and one day obliterate everything that stood against her beliefs. Zoe is infamous for getting into bar brawls, being one of the top troublemakers at the Adventurers' Camp, and using underhanded tactics to snatch bounty Missions. She's become the town's bogeyman—mothers often use her name to scare unruly children into behaving. But despite her rough reputation, Zoe has earned a great deal of respect and admiration. She's won "Best Vanguard Captain" and "Best Adventure Com Panion" multiple times at the camp, and she's even the female lead in a Romance novel written by bestselling author Smith. In his book, Fluttering Heart, there's a line that says, "The lady is like a rainbow—you only believe such beauty exists when you see it." It’s a sentiment that captures how those who admire Zoe truly feel.

description: Launches attacks on ennemies that enter its alert zone during rebels invasions.

title: Enlistment Office
description: When the number of injured soldiers exceeds the capacity limit of the Infirmary, the Enlistment Office will recruit reserves to replace some of the soldiers you've lost in battle. Recruit from your reserve by expending Loyalty and it will begin to re-accumulate. Factors affecting the Loyalty rate: - The lower your current Loyalty, the faster it will accumulate. - The fewer the severely injured in the Infirmary, the faster it will accumulate. - The more reserves (excluding reserves that can be enlisted immediately) in the Enlistment Office, the faster it will accumulate. Please note, Loyalty will stop increasing after reaching a certain limit. You can obtain Lovalty by collecting rewards from daily missions or gathering if the reserve in the Enlistment Office is not empty. You will get more as your Town Center level Increases. The Enlistment Office capacity is 400% of the Infirmary’s capacity.

title: Hero Hall
description: This is where you use Platinum and Gold keys to recruit Heroes to your team. Platinum keys are used to open Advanced recruitment chests while Gold keys are used to open Epic recruitment chests. Awards from the chests are Heroes, Hero Shards, Skill Books, Hero XP, and a variety of speedups and ressources.

title: House 1
description: These buildings house your Residents giving them a place to rest, relax, and sleep. As of this writing, a maximum of eight Houses can be built. As you upgrade the Houses and furniture inside them, the amount of Residents that can join your town increases up to a maximum of 32. Upgrading the Houses increases Resident Sleep Quality, Comfort, Mood, and Warmth along with a boost in power. You will need to max out the upgrades of certain furniture inside the building before being able to upgrade the building to the next level. Deleted: Keeping these buildings and the furniture inside them upgraded as much as you can is important for the health and happiness of your Residents. Until you get your Clinic built, your Residents will come back here if they get sick.

title: Iron Mine
description: This building produces iron and is the fourth Production building you will open. furniture inside this building are: Anvil, Foundry Table, Changin Room, Garbage Station, Coat Roak, Cooling Pool.

title: Conquerors' Camp
description: If you've reached your maximum amount of offline Idle time, a chest will appear above the main conquest page that you can directly receive your Idle rewards from. Otherwise, tapping The Conquerors' Camp will take you to Conquest mode.

title: Sawmill
description: This building produces wood and is the first Production building you will open. furniture inside this building are: Workbench, Design Bench, Steam Engine, Handbasin, Grinding wheel, Changing Room.

title: Quarry
description: This building produces stone and is the third Production building you will open. furniture inside this building are: Sorting Station, Stone Crusher, Changing Room, Pump , Shower Room, Water Wheel.

title: Mill
description: This building produces food and this the second Production building you will open. furniture inside this building are: Workbench, Rest Area, Oven, Millstone, Threshing Machine, Tool Rack.

title: Clinic
description: Once built, this is where your Survivors go to recover when they are sick. Upgrading this building and the furniture inside will improve the efficacy of your treatments, reduce Healing time, and increase the wellness restored by each treatment along with boosting your power.

title: Arena
description: This is where you will go to test your PVP mettle against other Governors. Bring your strongest Heroes and climb the Ranks. Challenging and winning against other Governor awards you Arena points. You will not lose points if you lose. Nor will you gain or lose points by winning or losing if another Governor challenges you. To gain Arena points, YOU must initiate the challenge. Rewards for your performance in the Arena are handed out daily and weekly, with the Arena seasons being reset every week. Winning in the Arena also gets you Arena Tokens which can be used in the Arena Store.

title: Watchtower
description: In this building, you will find Intelligence missions you can complete. These consist of rescuing Residents , hunting beasts, or having your Heroes battle their way through an investigation of a building. You can upgrade the Watchtower by completing the required amount of missions shown at the bottom left of the screen. It will upgrade to a maximum of level 20. Upgrading the Watchtower allows for more missions to be found during refreshes along with better quality missions. Better quality missions reward you with better prizes. Once you have completed all the missions available, you will need to wait until the reset to do more. Always make sure to complete these as much as you can. The prizes are more than worth it.

title: Monument
description: Tapping this displays a list of Zone missions and Alliance missions that can be completed. Reading the descriptions of the missions let's you know what the Zone or your Alliance needs to do to complete the mission. Rewards for these are typically very good, so it's an idea to try and complete as many of these as you can.

title: Suggestion Box
description: The Suggestion Box is split between two tabs: Letters and SOS. Suggestions Paying attention to the Letters gives you an idea of what your Residents are happy about, or not so happy about. If a Resident isn't happy about something, their mood drops and your Governor Approval Rating (GAR) will drop. So making sure you take care of the unhappy suggestions is very important. SOS Every now and then you will be called upon to make a decision to settle an issue in your town. Depending on the choices you make to resolve the issue, your GAR will either rise or fall. Do your best to keep your GAR high to keep your Residents happy and to get the best daily rewards.
